properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js@1.1.7 (SHA family implementation, including legacy SHA-1) ships in the demo React app's dependency tree. No direct call site found in the app source itself.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live crypto in the application: the XRPL private-key provider derives a Web3Auth key into an XRP Ledger account using ECDSA on secp256k1 (generateSeed with algorithm "ecdsa-secp256k1" and Wallet.fromSecret with ECDSA.secp256k1). The three root-lockfile sites are the tiny-secp256k1 dependency the build ships. Classical, Shor-vulnerable; XRPL itself mandates this curve, so changeable here only insofar as the ledger allows.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: evp_bytestokey is a transitive dependency (pulled in via the crypto-browserify/browserify stack) that implements OpenSSL's legacy EVP_BytesToKey single-round MD5 key derivation. No direct call site found in the application source; it ships in the demo app's dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: bcryptjs@2.4.3 (pure-JS bcrypt password hashing KDF) is declared in the root package-lock.json. Whether any first-party code calls it is a separate question the inventory does not settle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: node-forge@1.4.0 (RSA key generation/encryption, X.509, TLS primitives in pure JS) ships in the demo React app's dependency tree. Shor-vulnerable RSA available in the shipped library; no direct RSA call site found in the demo app source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves@1.9.1 provides the Ed25519 implementation shipped in both the demo React app and the x402 test server. The first-party package also imports Ed25519 (base-provider/utils.ts), so this library is the likely backing implementation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves@1.9.1 also provides the P-256 (secp256r1) implementation in the demo React app's dependency tree; no P-256 call site found in the demo app source itself.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes@1.8.0 provides SHA-256 (and the SHA-2/3 families) in the demo React app's dependency tree; the first-party SDK also imports from @noble/hashes.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/ciphers@1.3.0 provides AES-GCM in the vite demo app's dependency tree. AES-GCM is symmetric AE — not itself Shor-vulnerable, but its key comes from a quantum-vulnerable agreement/KDF path; posture depends on how the key is derived.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/ciphers@1.3.0 provides ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD in the vite demo app's dependency tree. Symmetric AE, quantum-resistant in practice; recorded because it is what encrypts data once keys are agreed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Key-management infrastructure: @azure/keyvault-secrets ^4.9.0 is a declared workspace dependency (root package-lock.json), so the build ships a cloud-KMS/secrets-manager client. No first-party import found in the scanned source — likely a transitive/runtime-config-reachable dependency. Azure Key Vault is where managed keys and secrets would live; the vault's own supported algorithms (RSA, EC HSM SKUs) are observable here, replaceable only by Azure. Recorded as infrastructure presence.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl (XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox, X25519/Ed25519 via NaCl) ships in the x402-test-server's dependency tree. Crypto provider presence — decides what algorithms the demo server can use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: jose (JWS/JWE/JWT/JWK implementation — JOSE stack) ships in the vue demo, the x402 test server and the root workspace lockfiles. Its algorithm support (RSA, ECDSA, ECDH-ES key agreement) is what the demos can offer for JWT signing/encryption.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider: @noble/hashes (SHA-2, SHA-3, BLAKE, Keccak, RIPEMD) ships in the react and vite demo dependency trees — the hash implementation available to those builds. No first-party import found in the scanned source; the demos reach it transitively.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider: @noble/curves (secp256k1, P-256, ed25519, X25519 and other curves) ships in the react and vite demo dependency trees. Same library whose Ed25519/P-256/secp256k1 algorithms are recorded as separate algorithm objects; this row is the provider facet.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider: @noble/ciphers (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Salsa) ships in the vite demo app's dependency tree — the symmetric-AE implementation available to that build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider: node-forge@1.4.0 (pure-JS RSA, X.509, TLS, PKCS) ships in the react demo's dependency tree. Library facet of the RSA/X.509 objects recorded from the same lockfile; available in the shipped library even without a first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider: sha.js@2.4.12 (streaming SHA-1/SHA-2 family, including legacy SHA-1) ships in the react demo's dependency tree — a transitive dep of the browser crypto stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider: bcryptjs@2.4.3 in the root lockfile — the library facet of the bcrypt algorithm object (ALG-2384a3f4) recorded from the same dependency. Kept as a separate row: the CBOM records both the component and the capability it provides.
